title: Pull a seized compression olive off a copper pipe
instruction: Turn the fitted olive puller to free the brass ring, lift it clear, and slide the spare ring onto the pipe to check the fit.
context: When servicing a compression fitting, removing the old olive allows the pipe stub to be retained.
setup: A copper tube model stands vertically from a base with a brass olive retained at its end. A crossbar puller is already coaxially engaged. A spare brass ring rests on a staging peg beside the pipe. The robot can lift and park the extractor and old ring away from the original tube.
scoring: 0.5 when the extractor breaks the old olive free and parks it clear of the original tube. Full credit when the spare ring is aligned to within 2 mm of that same tube and inserted over 22 mm.
reset_notes: Return the extractor, both ring positions and the transfer guides to their initial positions. Leave the spare ring on its staging peg.
fidelity: The screw-lead constraint transmits the crossbar rotation to the spent olive. The tool begins pre-engaged. Contact-gated guides constrain the extractor and replacement-ring transfer, and the spare ring has physical clearance around the original tube.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.00 in 1,200 steps. Scripted dual-YAM demo: 1.00 in 867 steps.
